claims.claim: The letter is addressed to the brethren throughout Asia and Phrygia, who share the same faith and hope of redemption as the writers.
The letter describes the persecution and martyrdoms at Lyons in 177 CE, under the emperor Marcus Aurelius.

The text survives only through the fourth-century church historian Eusebius, who presents it as a letter from those communities to Christians in Asia Minor; it is found in his Ecclesiastical History V.1.1–2.8.
Some internal evidence suggests the text may have been reworked before Eusebius, and there are questions about the accuracy of the original writers; this is a scholarly question, not a settled one.
Blandina is featured in the letter's story, which is also titled as including the story of the blessed Blandina.
Local persecutions of this period were largely local affairs, with provincial governors responsible for deciding how to handle Christians accused by their neighbours.
